scope: Historically significant cults, mystery traditions, occult/esoteric organizations, Satanic movements, modern anti-religious currents and deity-centered traditions that require a different analytical layer from the main religion registry.

records.name: Moloch / Molek
records.period: Iron Age Levant and later biblical/antique reception
records.field: Phoenician and Canaanite religious environments and biblical Judah/Israel
records.deity_or_concept: The Hebrew Bible uses mōlek; scholarship disputes whether this primarily denotes a deity, a sacrificial rite, or both.
evidence: Tophet references in the Hebrew Bible
Punic molk inscriptions and archaeological evidence
Greek and Roman-era discussions of child sacrifice
records.practice: The biblical tradition condemns offerings of children through fire; archaeological interpretation of Tophet deposits and Punic molk terminology remains debated.
records.modern_reception: Moloch became a powerful literary and political symbol of destructive institutions and sacrifice of the vulnerable; modern Moloch movements are not established continuations of the ancient cult.
records.integrity: The identity of Moloch is contested; do not present the popular horned idol image as an archaeological portrait.

records.name: Cult of Saturn / Saturnalia
records.field: Roman religion, agricultural cults and Italian religious traditions
records.deity_or_concept: Saturn was associated with agriculture, sowing, abundance and an idealized Golden Age.
records.practice: The Saturnalia festival involved public sacrifice, feasting, gift-giving, role inversion and suspension of some ordinary social conventions.
institutions: Temple of Saturn in the Roman Forum
texts: Roman antiquarian and literary sources including Macrobius, Saturnalia
records.legacy: Later occult and esoteric writers associated Saturn with time, limitation, melancholy and occult symbolism, but this is a later reception rather than the ordinary Roman cult.
records.integrity: 'Saturnism' is not an established historical name for a continuous Roman religion; modern Saturnian occultism must be recorded separately from Roman Saturn worship.

records.name: Eleusinian Mysteries
records.period: c. 1600 BCE origins of Eleusis; institutionalized Greek mysteries through antiquity; ended in late antiquity
records.goal: Initiation promised privileged sacred knowledge and a better relationship to death and the afterlife, though the central secret was deliberately not written down.
records.integrity: The exact content of the secret initiation cannot be reconstructed with certainty.

records.name: Dionysian / Bacchic Mysteries
records.period: Classical and Hellenistic antiquity; Roman Bacchic developments
records.integrity: The Dionysian world included multiple local practices; it was not a single centralized church.

records.name: Roman Mithraic Mysteries
practice: ritual use of caves or cave-like mithraea
places: mithraea across Italy, Gaul, Britain, Danube provinces and Rome
records.integrity: Roman Mithraism should not simply be equated with the much older Iranian deity Mithra; historical connection is debated and the Roman cult developed its own form.

records.name: Cult of Isis in the Greco-Roman World
records.field: Egyptian religion transformed through Mediterranean syncretism
themes: salvation and initiation in some interpretations
records.integrity: The Roman cult was neither identical to pharaonic-period Egyptian worship nor simply a precursor to Christianity.

records.name: Roman Imperial Cult
records.focus: ritual recognition of emperors, imperial family and Roman political order
records.importance: Shows how religion, sovereignty, public loyalty and political legitimacy can form a single institutional layer.
records.integrity: Imperial cult varied substantially by region and period; it was not simply a uniform demand to regard every emperor as a god.

records.name: Orphic Traditions
records.period: evidence from Classical Greece onward, with roots attributed to older mythic material
records.integrity: 'Orphism' is a modern scholarly umbrella for diverse materials rather than a single centrally organized ancient church.

records.name: Hermeticism
records.period: Hellenistic/Roman Egypt; major Renaissance and modern revivals
practice: theurgical or magical practices in later Hermeticism
astrology and alchemy in later traditions
records.legacy: Hermeticism became a major source for Renaissance magic, alchemy and later occult revival movements.
records.integrity: Ancient Hermetism, Renaissance Hermeticism and modern occult Hermeticism are historically related but not identical.

records.name: Rosicrucianism
records.legacy: Rosicrucian imagery and claims became foundational to later Western occult organizations.
records.integrity: The original manifestos do not establish an ancient secret order in the modern sense; later organizations constructed institutional lineages around them.

records.name: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
records.legacy: Its ritual system strongly influenced modern ceremonial magic, Thelema and later occult revival groups.
records.sources_note: Cambridge and Oxford scholarship identifies it as a pivotal institutional site for modern ritual magic.

records.name: Thelema
texts: Liber AL vel Legis / The Book of the Law
records.core_idea: Thelema centers on discovery and fulfillment of True Will and a new religious-magical framework associated with the New Aeon.
records.legacy: Major modern esoteric movement with influence on occultism, alternative spirituality and popular culture.
records.integrity: Thelema is distinct from generic occultism and from Satanism even where imagery or practices overlap.

records.name: Ordo Templi Orientis
records.period: founded around 1904–1906; reorganized under Crowley in the 20th century
records.field: European and North American occult revival
records.structure: graded initiatory order with lodges and affiliated bodies
records.legacy: One of the most influential surviving institutional networks of modern ceremonial occultism.
records.integrity: Its history contains changing organizational structures, disputed succession claims and multiple periods of reorganization.

records.name: Theosophical Society
records.field: Victorian spiritualism, occult revival, comparative religion
organizations: Theosophical Society in America and other branches
records.legacy: Major conduit for the movement of South Asian and esoteric concepts into Western occult milieus.
records.integrity: Theosophical claims about ancient masters and hidden histories are religious/esoteric claims, not automatically historical evidence.

records.name: Anthroposophy
records.field: European Theosophy, idealism and esoteric Christianity
records.legacy: Influenced education, agriculture, medicine and arts as well as esoteric spirituality.
records.integrity: Institutional applications and spiritual doctrines should be separately documented from empirical claims.

records.name: Church of Satan
records.field: 1960s American counterculture and modern occult milieu
records.worldview: Largely atheistic/non-theistic Satanism in which Satan functions primarily as a symbol of individualism, pride, liberty and opposition to conventional religious morality.
records.organization: Church with formal priesthood and organizational hierarchy
branches_and_schisms: Temple of Set emerged from a 1975 schism involving Michael Aquino
records.integrity: Modern Satanism is not evidence that historical Christians accused of Satanism actually worshipped Satan. Scholarly research places coherent self-identified Satanism around the turn of the 20th century, with LaVey's Church as a major codification in 1966.

records.name: The Satanic Temple
records.field: contemporary American religious pluralism, secularism and activism
records.worldview: Non-theistic Satanic symbolism used to advocate individual autonomy, bodily autonomy, secularism, pluralism, compassion and skepticism of arbitrary authority.
practice: rituals and ceremonies framed as symbolic or religious expression
records.public_role: Uses religious-liberty and church-state disputes as part of its public activism.
records.integrity: Distinct from the Church of Satan despite shared Satanic symbolism.

records.name: Temple of Set
records.deity_or_principle: Set, understood within Setian theology as a metaphysical and initiatory principle rather than simply the Christian devil.
texts: The Book of Coming Forth by Night
records.integrity: Scholars debate whether it should be categorized as Satanism; it is historically descended from the Church of Satan but self-understanding emphasizes Setian rather than Satanic identity.
sources: Oxford scholarship on the Temple of Set and post-Satanism

records.name: Order of Nine Angles
texts: The Black Book of Satan and related ONA corpus
records.integrity: Requires a distinct risk-aware research layer: document its ideology and history without romanticizing or operationalizing extremist material. Claims of ancient lineage are treated as claims unless independently supported.
sources: Cambridge/Oxford scholarship on Satanism and modern occult movements

records.name: Process Church of the Final Judgment
records.organization: communal religious movement with centers in several countries
records.legacy: Important case in the history of modern Satanism and counterculture, despite its relatively short institutional life.
records.integrity: Later conspiracy narratives often greatly exaggerate its relationship to crime; historical reconstruction should use documentary evidence.

records.name: Freemasonry
records.period: modern institutional form early 18th century; older operative masonry and legends provide antecedents
texts: Anderson's Constitutions and jurisdiction-specific ritual/constitutional materials
records.legacy: Major global fraternal network and important source environment for later occult and esoteric organizations.
records.integrity: Freemasonry is not itself synonymous with occultism, Satanism or a secret government; its secrecy is principally ritual/private rather than proof of alleged conspiracies.

records.name: Militant Anti-Religious / State-Attempted Secularization Movements
records.field: Enlightenment materialism, revolutionary socialism, Marxist-Leninist states and other secularizing projects
examples: Cultural Revolution attacks on religious institutions
institutions: League of Militant Godless in Soviet history
records.integrity: Anti-religion, atheism, secularism and anti-clericalism are distinct categories; not every atheist or secularist is anti-religious.

research_status: All records contain substantive historical information. Disputed claims are explicitly marked rather than filled with invented certainty.
